candidates.text: The representative ESA (rear combination lamp with its LED modules, PCB, wiring and connector) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 of this Regulation (emissions and immunity in configurations other than REESS charging mode) for ESA type approval to be granted; paragraph 7 does not apply because the lamp is not used in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.
candidates.test_case: Review the test reports for radiated and conducted emission and immunity tests (paras 6.5, 6.6, 6.8, Annex 10) and confirm that all results meet paragraph 6.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an ESA seeking component/STU approval under R10, and approval depends on meeting paragraph 6.

candidates.text: Since the ESA is (part of) a light source, the ESA shall have the documentation specified in paragraph 3.2.10; without it, approval of the ESA under Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.
candidates.test_case: Check that the approval file contains either an R37/R99/R128 approval number or a Technical Service non-interchangeability report for the LED light source.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED modules on the PCB are light sources integrated in the ESA.

candidates.text: In case of non-replaceable LED modules, a test report by a designated Technical Service shall be provided stating that the LED module/ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128.
candidates.test_case: Have the Technical Service inspect the LED module interface and compare it with the R37/R99/R128 light source caps, then issue the report.
candidates.applies_because: The profile states the LED modules are non-replaceable, so the non-interchangeability route applies.

candidates.text: In case of a replaceable LED light source approved under Regulation No. 128, the approval number granted to this light source under Regulation No. 128 shall be specified for the ESA.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the R128 approval number is quoted in the application and matches the marking on the light source.
candidates.applies_because: The open option of a replaceable R128 LED light source requires the R128 approval reference.

candidates.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every rear lamp (ESA) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
candidates.test_case: Inspect production samples for the presence of the R10 approval mark.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp with LED modules on PCB is an ESA seeking component/STU approval under R10.

candidates.text: The international approval mark shall be affixed in a conspicuous and easily accessible place on the ESA, as specified on the approval communication form.
candidates.test_case: Compare the mark location on the lamp with the location stated on the communication form.
candidates.applies_because: Paragraph 5.2.2 applies the mark of paragraph 5.3 to approved ESAs such as this lamp.

candidates.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E", followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for the circled "E" and the correct country number.
candidates.applies_because: Defines the content of the approval mark required on the approved ESA.

candidates.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for "10R-" followed by the approval number to the right of the circle.
candidates.applies_because: Defines the content and layout of the approval mark required on the approved ESA.

candidates.text: The R10 approval markings on the ESA (rear lamp) need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Check on the drawing that the mark is on the lamp, accepting a location hidden when the lamp is installed.
candidates.applies_because: This permission covers where the lamp's R10 mark may be placed, e.g. on the housing hidden after installation.

candidates.text: The ESA (rear combination lamp with its LED modules, PCB and wiring) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, can comply with the requirements of UN R10.
candidates.test_case: Review the design and confirm that all applicable R10 ESA tests are passed.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an ESA fitted to M1 vehicles.

candidates.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated emissions, conducted emissions, immunity to radiated disturbances and immunity to conducted disturbances.
candidates.test_case: Check that the test plan and reports cover the radiated and conducted emission and immunity tests.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is submitted for ESA approval under R10.

candidates.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 30 to 75 MHz band shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz (Appendix 6).
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 7 (CISPR 25 ALSE) broadband measurement from 30 to 75 MHz and compare with the limit line.
candidates.applies_because: The LED electronics are an ESA subject to broadband emission limits.

candidates.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 52 to 63 dBµV/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 6).
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 7 broadband measurement from 75 to 400 MHz and compare with the limit line.
candidates.applies_because: The LED electronics are an ESA subject to broadband emission limits.

candidates.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall be constant at 63 dBµV/m.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 7 broadband measurement from 400 to 1,000 MHz and compare with 63 dBµV/m.
candidates.applies_because: The LED electronics are an ESA subject to broadband emission limits.

candidates.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
candidates.test_case: Confirm that all measured broadband emission levels lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion for the lamp's broadband emission test.

candidates.text: In case the ESA includes an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz (e.g. active switch-mode/PWM driver or microcontroller), the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit measured by the method of Annex 8 in the 30 to 75 MHz band shall be 52 to 42 dBµV/m, decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz (Appendix 7).
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 narrowband measurement (average detector) from 30 to 75 MHz and compare with the limit line.
candidates.applies_because: An active LED driver makes the lamp subject to narrowband emission limits.

candidates.text: In case the ESA includes an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit measured by the method of Annex 8 in the 75 to 400 MHz band shall be 42 to 53 dBµV/m, increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz (Appendix 7).
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 narrowband measurement from 75 to 400 MHz and compare with the limit line.
candidates.applies_because: An active LED driver makes the lamp subject to narrowband emission limits.

candidates.text: In case the ESA includes an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz, the ESA narrowband radiated emission limit measured by the method of Annex 8 in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall be constant at 53 dBµV/m.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 8 narrowband measurement from 400 to 1,000 MHz and compare with 53 dBµV/m.
candidates.applies_because: An active LED driver makes the lamp subject to narrowband emission limits.

candidates.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband emission value, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
candidates.test_case: Confirm that all measured narrowband levels lie below the limit line across 30 to 1,000 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion for the lamp's narrowband emission test.

candidates.text: Where the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz (e.g. passive resistor/linear LED drive), the ESA shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.6.2 and Annex 8 (narrowband emission).
candidates.test_case: Review the circuit schematic and component list to confirm that no oscillator or switching above 9 kHz is present.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED drive may be passive (open option).

candidates.text: The transient conducted emission of the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes of Table 1.
candidates.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 transient emissions on the supply lines at switch-off/switching per Annex 10.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is supplied from the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system ESA, the positive transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall not exceed +75 V.
candidates.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 positive pulse amplitude on the 12 V supply line.
candidates.applies_because: This limit applies if the lamp is a 12 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system ESA, the negative transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall not exceed -100 V.
candidates.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 negative pulse amplitude on the 12 V supply line.
candidates.applies_because: This limit applies if the lamp is a 12 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 24 V system ESA, the positive transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall not exceed +150 V.
candidates.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 positive pulse amplitude on the 24 V supply line.
candidates.applies_because: This limit applies if the lamp is a 24 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 24 V system ESA, the negative transient conducted emission pulse amplitude shall not exceed -450 V.
candidates.test_case: Measure the ISO 7637-2 negative pulse amplitude on the 24 V supply line.
candidates.applies_because: This limit applies if the lamp is a 24 V supply variant.

candidates.text: An ESA that is not switched, contains no switches or does not include an inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
candidates.test_case: Review the schematic for switches, switching elements and inductive loads to justify the exemption.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED drive may have no switching or inductive load.

candidates.text: The immunity of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation shall be tested by method(s) chosen from Annex 9, at the test severity of Table 2a in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band and at the minimum test level of Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Annex 9 radiated immunity test(s) at the Table 2a/2b levels while monitoring the lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp and rear position lamp are immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: If tested by the stripline method, the ESA shall withstand 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz range for over 90 per cent of the band.
candidates.test_case: Perform the stripline test at 60 V/m from 20 to 400 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies to the lamp's radiated immunity test if the stripline method is chosen.

candidates.text: If tested by the TEM cell method, the ESA shall withstand 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz range for over 90 per cent of the band.
candidates.test_case: Perform the TEM cell test at 75 V/m from 20 to 200 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies to the lamp's radiated immunity test if the TEM cell method is chosen.

candidates.text: If tested by bulk current injection (BCI), the ESA shall withstand 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz range for over 90 per cent of the band.
candidates.test_case: Perform the BCI test at 60 mA from 20 to 400 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies to the lamp's radiated immunity test if the BCI method is chosen.

candidates.text: If tested in an ALSE, the ESA shall withstand 30 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz and 10 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, for over 90 per cent of the band.
candidates.test_case: Perform the ALSE test at 30 V/m (80–2,000 MHz) and 10 V/m (2–6 GHz) and monitor the lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: These levels apply to the lamp's radiated immunity test if the ALSE method is chosen.

candidates.text: If tested in a reverberation chamber, the ESA shall withstand 21 V/m from LUF to 2,000 MHz and 7 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz, for over 90 per cent of the band.
candidates.test_case: Perform the reverberation chamber test at 21 V/m and 7 V/m and monitor the lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: These levels apply to the lamp's radiated immunity test if the reverberation chamber method is chosen.

candidates.text: If tested by the stripline method, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz range shall be 50 V/m.
candidates.test_case: Verify from the test log that no frequency was tested below 50 V/m.
candidates.applies_because: This minimum level applies to the lamp's stripline radiated immunity test.

candidates.text: If tested by the TEM cell method, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 200 MHz range shall be 62.5 V/m.
candidates.test_case: Verify from the test log that no frequency was tested below 62.5 V/m.
candidates.applies_because: This minimum level applies to the lamp's TEM cell radiated immunity test.

candidates.text: If tested by BCI, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz range shall be 50 mA.
candidates.test_case: Verify from the test log that no frequency was tested below 50 mA.
candidates.applies_because: This minimum level applies to the lamp's BCI radiated immunity test.

candidates.text: If tested in an ALSE, the minimum test level over the whole band shall be 25 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz and 8 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
candidates.test_case: Verify from the test log that the minimum levels of 25 V/m and 8 V/m were met.
candidates.applies_because: These minimum levels apply to the lamp's ALSE radiated immunity test.

candidates.text: If tested in a reverberation chamber, the minimum test level over the whole band shall be 18 V/m from LUF to 2,000 MHz and 6 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
candidates.test_case: Verify from the test log that the minimum levels of 18 V/m and 6 V/m were met.
candidates.applies_because: These minimum levels apply to the lamp's reverberation chamber radiated immunity test.

candidates.text: During the radiated immunity tests of Annex 9 there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity related functions (stop lamp and rear position lamp light output).
candidates.test_case: Monitor the stop and rear position lamp outputs (camera/photodetector) during exposure for any flicker, dimming or switch-off.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp and rear position lamp are listed immunity-related functions.

candidates.text: The immunity of the ESA to transients conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 (starting profile) and ISO 7637-2 (pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b) as described in Annex 10, at the levels of Tables 3a and 3b. The results shall meet the ISO 16750-1 functional status classification for the starting profile and the ISO 7637-1 FPSC for the pulses.
candidates.test_case: Apply the starting profile and the ISO 7637-2 pulses to the supply lines and classify the lamp behaviour.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is supplied from the vehicle 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: Where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started by a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand starting profile level II (12 V and 24 V) with 10 pulses. The functional status shall be class B for immunity related functions that must be operational during engine start, class C for other immunity related functions, and class D for functions not related to immunity related functions (e.g. reversing lamp).
candidates.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile level II 10 times and assess the functional status of each lamp function.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be fitted to ICE M1 vehicles, and its stop and rear position lamps are immunity-related.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 1 at -75 V for 500 pulses with FPSC III for both immunity related and non-immunity related functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 at -75 V, 500 pulses, and verify FPSC III.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 12 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 1 at -450 V for 500 pulses with FPSC III for both immunity related and non-immunity related functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 1 at -450 V, 500 pulses, and verify FPSC III.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 24 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2a at +37 V for 500 pulses, with FPSC I for immunity related functions (stop/rear position lamp) and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 2a at +37 V, 500 pulses, and verify that the stop and position lamps are unaffected.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 12 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2a at +37 V for 500 pulses, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 2a at +37 V, 500 pulses, and verify the FPSC per function.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 24 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2b at +10 V for 10 pulses, with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 2b at +10 V, 10 pulses, and verify the FPSC per function.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 12 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 2b at +20 V for 10 pulses, with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 2b at +20 V, 10 pulses, and verify the FPSC per function.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 24 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3a at -112 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 3a at -112 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 12 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3a at -150 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 3a at -150 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 24 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 12 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3b at +75 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 3b at +75 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 12 V supply variant.

candidates.text: For a 24 V system, the ESA shall withstand pulse 3b at +150 V for 1 h, with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for other functions.
candidates.test_case: Apply pulse 3b at +150 V for 1 h and monitor the lamp outputs.
candidates.applies_because: This level applies if the lamp is a 24 V supply variant.

candidates.text: ESAs approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
candidates.test_case: Take series samples of the rear lamp and repeat the paragraph 6 emission and immunity tests against the type-approval results.
candidates.applies_because: The LED rear lamp is an ESA approved under R10 and series units must keep meeting paragraph 6.

candidates.text: For a production ESA taken from the series, the measured broadband electromagnetic emission levels shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1 (62 to 52 dBµV/m in 30–75 MHz, 52 to 63 dBµV/m in 75–400 MHz, 63 dBµV/m in 400–1,000 MHz) by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
candidates.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emission of a series lamp per Annex 7 and check that levels are at most 4 dB above the 6.5.2.1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED electronics are an ESA subject to the broadband emission limits, and this sets the tolerance for series units.

candidates.text: For a production ESA taken from the series, the measured narrowband electromagnetic emission levels shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 (52 to 42 dBµV/m in 30–75 MHz, 42 to 53 dBµV/m in 75–400 MHz, 53 dBµV/m in 400–1,000 MHz) by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
candidates.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emission of a series lamp per Annex 8 and check that levels are at most 4 dB above the 6.6.2.1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED electronics are an ESA subject to the narrowband emission limits, and this sets the tolerance for series units.

candidates.text: A production ESA taken from the series shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road users (e.g. stop lamp or rear position lamp malfunction) when subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the ESA immunity reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
candidates.test_case: Apply radiated immunity testing per Annex 9 at 80 % of the 6.8.2.1 levels to a series lamp and monitor the stop and rear position lamp outputs for any degradation.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp and rear position lamp are immunity-related functions of this ESA, so series units must meet radiated immunity at 80 % of the reference level.

candidates.text: A production component or STU taken from the series shall show no degradation of performance of immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) when subjected to conducted transient disturbances up to the levels given in paragraph 6.9.1.
candidates.test_case: Apply the Annex 10 conducted transient pulses at the 6.9.1 levels to a series lamp on its 12 V or 24 V supply and verify that the stop and rear position lamp functions are not degraded.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an ESA component/STU with immunity-related functions supplied from the 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: A production component or STU taken from the series shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1.
candidates.test_case: Measure conducted transient emission of a series lamp on its supply lines per Annex 10 and compare the results with the 6.7.1 levels.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED electronics are an ESA whose conducted transient emissions on the 12/24 V supply lines are limited.

candidates.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz): 30-75 MHz: E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30); 75-400 MHz: E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75); 400-1,000 MHz: E = 63. This applies unless the broadband exception of paragraph 6.10 covers the lamp's drive electronics (e.g. a passive resistor/linear LED drive).
candidates.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emission of the lamp per Annex 7 (ALSE, 30-1,000 MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth) and compare the peak values with the Appendix 6 limit line.
candidates.applies_because: The LED modules on PCB form an ESA approved under R10, and paragraph 6.5.2.1 sets these Appendix 6 broadband limits for ESAs.

candidates.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (oscillator, switch-mode or PWM, microcontroller or data bus), the narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the rear lamp ESA, when measured by the method of Annex 8 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits E (dBµV/m) at frequency F (MHz): 30-75 MHz: E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30); 75-400 MHz: E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75); 400-1,000 MHz: E = 53.
candidates.test_case: Measure radiated narrowband emission of the lamp per Annex 8 (ALSE, 30-1,000 MHz, 120 kHz bandwidth, average detector) and compare the values with the Appendix 7 limit line.
candidates.applies_because: Paragraph 6.6.2.1 sets these Appendix 7 narrowband limits for ESAs, and they bind a lamp whose electronics are not covered by the paragraph 6.10 exception for ESAs without oscillators.

candidates.text: The broadband electromagnetic emissions of the ESA (rear lamp LED modules and drive circuitry) shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 7.
candidates.test_case: Verify in the test report that broadband radiated emission testing of the lamp was performed to CISPR 25.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp's LED PCB is an ESA approved under R10, and its broadband emission is measured by the Annex 7 method referenced in paragraph 6.5.1.

candidates.text: During the broadband emission test, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load.
candidates.test_case: Operate the lamp with all functions energised at nominal supply during the emission scan and record the operating mode in the report.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the operating state in which the lamp's emissions must stay within limits, e.g. rear position, stop and reversing functions energised.

candidates.text: For an ESA other than one involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
candidates.test_case: Perform the radiated emission measurement in an ALSE per CISPR 25 Clause 6.4 and check the setup against the standard.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp is a 12/24 V ESA not involved in REESS charging.

candidates.text: As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE), the ESA may be measured on an open area test site (OATS) complying with CISPR 16-1-4.
candidates.test_case: If an OATS is used, verify the site's CISPR 16-1-4 compliance documentation.
candidates.applies_because: This permitted alternative measuring location applies to the lamp ESA test.

candidates.text: The ESA broadband emission limits (paragraph 6.5.2.1: 62 to 52 dBµV/m over 30–75 MHz decreasing logarithmically, 52 to 63 dBµV/m over 75–400 MHz increasing logarithmically, 63 dBµV/m constant over 400–1,000 MHz) apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements in an ALSE or OATS.
candidates.test_case: Scan 30–1,000 MHz in both polarisations and check that all quasi-peak readings stay below the limit curve.
candidates.applies_because: These are the pass limits for the lamp's broadband radiated emission, binding in particular when the drive electronics are active (switch-mode/PWM/microcontroller) and not exempted under 6.10.

candidates.text: The broadband limits are quasi-peak limits; if peak detectors are used, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
candidates.test_case: Where peak detection is used, verify that the limit was raised by 20 dB (per CISPR 12) when assessing compliance.
candidates.applies_because: This defines how the lamp's measured emission levels are compared against the type approval limits.

candidates.text: The maximum of the readings relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands shall be taken as the characteristic reading at the frequency at which the measurements were made.
candidates.test_case: Check that the test report takes the worst-case polarisation reading per band as the characteristic value compared with the limit.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the reading of the lamp's emission that is assessed against the limit.

candidates.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (not exempted under paragraph 6.10), the narrowband electromagnetic emissions of the rear lamp ESA shall be measured according to CISPR 25, unless otherwise stated in Annex 8.
candidates.test_case: Perform the narrowband radiated emission test on the lamp according to CISPR 25 and Annex 8, and check the results against the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp is an ESA (LED modules on PCB) whose narrowband emissions must meet paragraph 6.6 when tested by the Annex 8 method.

candidates.text: During the narrowband emission test, the rear lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load (e.g. rear position, stop and reversing functions energised).
candidates.test_case: Verify in the test plan and setup that all lamp functions are energised at nominal supply during the emission measurement.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the operating state in which the lamp's narrowband emission compliance is assessed.

candidates.text: The narrowband emission limits for the rear lamp ESA apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or an open area test site (OATS).
candidates.test_case: Scan radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz in an ALSE or OATS and confirm that no narrowband emission exceeds the limit.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the frequency range over which the lamp ESA must comply with the narrowband limits.

candidates.text: The narrowband emissions of the rear lamp ESA shall be evaluated with an average detector.
candidates.test_case: Check that the emission measurement report shows average-detector readings, and compare them with the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The detector type defines the measured quantity against which the lamp's narrowband limits are applied.

candidates.text: The rear lamp ESA may show compliance with the radiated immunity requirements using any combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided that together they cover the full frequency range of paragraph 3.1 of Annex 9 (20 to 6,000 MHz): absorber chamber test (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell test (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection test (ISO 11452-4), stripline test (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber test (ISO 11452-11).
candidates.test_case: Review the immunity test plan and reports to confirm that the selected ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp is an ESA with immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) and must undergo ESA immunity testing per Annex 9.

candidates.text: During the immunity test, the rear lamp ESA shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, with the stop lamp and rear position lamp functions operating.
candidates.test_case: Check in the test report and setup that the lamp is powered and its stop and rear position functions are activated and monitored throughout the exposure.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the operating state in which the lamp's immunity-related functions must withstand the radiated disturbance.

candidates.text: The rear lamp ESA shall be exposed to the radiated immunity disturbance over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps and dwell times according to ISO 11452-1.
candidates.test_case: Perform the immunity test across 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 step sizes and dwell times while monitoring the lamp functions.
candidates.applies_because: This is the frequency range of the electromagnetic stress the lamp ESA must withstand.

candidates.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be amplitude modulated (AM) with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth.
candidates.test_case: Verify the signal generator settings (AM, 1 kHz, 80 %) for 20 to 400 MHz and monitor the lamp for malfunction.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the modulation of the stress the lamp ESA must withstand in this band.

candidates.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulated type PM2, with Ton 3 µs and period 3,333 µs.
candidates.test_case: Verify the PM2 settings (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) for 2,700 to 3,100 MHz and monitor the lamp for malfunction.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the modulation of the stress the lamp ESA must withstand in this band.

candidates.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulated type PM3, with Ton 500 µs and period 1,000 µs.
candidates.test_case: Verify the PM3 settings (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) for 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz and monitor the lamp for malfunction.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the modulation of the stress the lamp ESA must withstand in these bands.

candidates.text: The ESA (rear lamp LED modules and drive circuitry) shall be immune to transient disturbances conducted along the 12/24 V supply lines when test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2 are applied to the supply lines and to the other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines (applies to the 12 V or 24 V version, whichever is supplied).
candidates.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to the supply and supply-connected lines of the lamp and check the lamp functions against the required functional status.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp is an ESA powered from the 12/24 V vehicle supply and performs immunity-related functions (stop and rear position lamp).

candidates.text: The ESA shall be immune to the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines and to the other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
candidates.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines and verify the stop, rear position and reversing functions behave as required.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is intended for M1 vehicles that may have a 12 V/24 V starter motor, so the cranking profile binds it.

candidates.text: In case the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12 V/24 V starter motor), the ESA is not subject to the starting profile test according to ISO 16750-2.
candidates.test_case: Check the approval documentation for a restriction of use to electric vehicles before omitting the starting profile test.
candidates.applies_because: This exemption applies to the lamp only if the manufacturer restricts its use to vehicles without a starter motor.

candidates.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on the 12/24 V supply lines and on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines shall be limited, as measured according to ISO 7637-2.
candidates.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emissions on the lamp supply lines per ISO 7637-2 while switching the lamp functions and compare against the applicable limits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's LED electronics are switched on the vehicle supply and can generate conducted transients onto the 12/24 V supply lines.

candidates.text: The lamp shall have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp drawing and sample to confirm there is a dedicated marking area large enough for all required markings.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp is a device of an approved R148 type.

candidates.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the markings visually and perform a rub/durability check to confirm legibility and permanence.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp carries R148 approval and other markings.

candidates.text: The dimension "a" of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the dimension "a" of the moulded or printed approval mark on the lamp.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp bears an R148 approval marking.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's approval marking must contain the E-mark.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4-6 digit sequential number and check it against the approval documentation.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's approval marking must contain the sequential approval number.

candidates.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking layout to confirm the sequential number sits adjacent to the circled E.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp bears the sequential number together with the E-mark.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the approved lamp functions per paragraph 3.2.4: R1 (in case of steady rear position lamp) or R2 (in case of variable intensity rear position lamp); S1 (in case of steady stop lamp) or S2 (in case of variable intensity stop lamp); and AR for the reversing lamp.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols and compare them with the approved functions and classes.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp integrates rear position, stop and reversing functions approved under R148.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall include the number of the Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits of the series of amendments in force at the time of approval (e.g. 148R01).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for "148R" followed by the correct series-of-amendments digits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is approved under UN R148.

candidates.text: In case the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, it shall bear a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
candidates.test_case: Check the design for side dependency and, if side-specific, inspect the marking for the horizontal arrow.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be side-specific (open option on mounting-side marking).

candidates.text: For the rear position lamp (and rear end-outline marker lamp) function, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the arrow orientation relative to the intended mounting side.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains a rear position lamp, which is also deemed a rear end-outline marker lamp.

candidates.text: In case the reversing lamp has a reduced light distribution for fitment of two reversing lamps, the horizontal mounting arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect that the arrow points outboard.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp may have a reduced light distribution (open option).

candidates.text: In case the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for "D" to the right of the relevant function symbol.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be part of an assembly of two independent lamps (open option).

candidates.text: In case the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for "Y" to the right of the relevant function symbol.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be part of an interdependent lamp system (open option).

candidates.text: In case the lamp (e.g. the reversing lamp) has a reduced light distribution per paragraph 1.1. of Annex 3, it shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
candidates.test_case: For the reduced-distribution variant, inspect the marking for the downward vertical arrow on a horizontal segment.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp may use the reduced light distribution option.

candidates.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the production sample for the presence of the complete approval marking.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an approved R148 device.

candidates.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the applicant's trade name or mark.
candidates.applies_because: Applies to every R148 lamp.

candidates.text: In case of non-replaceable LED light sources, the lamp is exempted from the marking of the light source category or categories.
candidates.test_case: Confirm the light sources are non-replaceable and that no category marking is needed.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp uses non-replaceable LED light sources.

candidates.text: The lamp shall bear a marking of its rated voltage(s) (e.g. 12V) or voltage range, because it has non-replaceable light sources (and, where applicable, an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking and compare it with the specification.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp has non-replaceable LED light sources and possibly variable intensity (R2/S2).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect each module for the applicant's trade name or mark.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable light source module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its specific identification code: the letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, plus additional symbols or characters where several non-identical modules are used. The module and lamp approval marks shall be from the same applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module for the MD code format and check the applicant against the lamp approval.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable light source module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each module shall bear its rated voltage(s) or voltage range.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module for the rated voltage marking.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable light source module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the MD identification code matching the module.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable light source module (open option).

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or voltage range.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage marking.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable light source module (open option).

candidates.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the external control unit for its identification number and manufacturer name.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may have external control gear declared as part of the lamp (open option).

candidates.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the light-emitting transparent part of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Review the assembly design to confirm the marked part cannot be separated from the outer lens.
candidates.applies_because: Defines where the lamp's approval marking must be located.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle, or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle (with the boot lid open if needed) to confirm the approval marking is visible.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is installed at the rear exterior of M1 vehicles.

candidates.text: If the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
candidates.test_case: Check whether the lens is detachable and, if so, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.
candidates.applies_because: Conditional on the design of the outer lens attachment of the lamp.

candidates.text: In case the outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the main body marking to confirm it lists only its own functions.
candidates.applies_because: Conditional on the outer lens being shared across several lamp types.

candidates.text: The approval marking, the trade name or mark, the rated voltage marking, the module identification code and voltage (for lamps with replaceable modules) and, where applicable, the external control gear identification shall be affixed on the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp assembly for the presence of all listed markings.
candidates.applies_because: Defines where the lamp's markings are affixed.

candidates.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the module markings (trade name, MD identification code, rated voltage) shall be affixed on the module itself.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module component for its markings.
candidates.applies_because: The light source may be a replaceable light source module (open option).

candidates.text: The trade name, light source category, rated voltage, light source module and control gear markings need not be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Confirm that only the approval marking is required to be visible when installed.
candidates.applies_because: This relaxation applies to the lamp's secondary markings.

candidates.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (R148 lamp functions and the R150 retro-reflector) comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number may be affixed, located anywhere on the lamp assembly subject to paragraphs 3.3.5.1.1 and 3.3.5.1.2.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the single combined approval mark and its content against the approvals granted.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp groups R148 functions with an R150 retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case a single approval mark is used, it shall be visible after installation of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle for visibility of the single approval mark.
candidates.applies_because: Condition for using a single approval mark on the grouped lamp.

candidates.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Review the assembly design to confirm the lens and retro-reflector cannot be removed independently of the marked part.
candidates.applies_because: Condition for using a single approval mark on the grouped lamp.

candidates.text: The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted (R148, R150).
candidates.test_case: Measure the mark component dimensions and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R148 and R150.
candidates.applies_because: Applies if the lamp carries a single combined R148/R150 approval mark.

candidates.text: Each lamp function submitted for approval (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall conform to the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148.
candidates.test_case: Review the approval test report to confirm that every applicable paragraph 4 and 5 requirement was verified for each function.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp is submitted for R148 approval for its R, S and AR functions.

candidates.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN R48 (series in force at application) that pertain to rear position, stop and reversing lamps for M1 vehicles shall be met where they can be verified at lamp type approval.
candidates.test_case: Check the lamp against the applicable R48 general and individual specifications, e.g. geometric visibility and colour, at component level.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is intended for installation on M1 vehicles under R48.

candidates.text: The lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by R148.
candidates.test_case: Perform a vibration/durability test, then re-verify photometry, colour and function.
candidates.applies_because: This general robustness requirement applies to every R148 lamp, including its housing, fasteners, PCB and optics.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp is approved as an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D', this is permitted for these functions; the reversing lamp function cannot be approved as 'D'.
candidates.test_case: Check that a 'D' marking, if used, appears only on the rear position and/or stop lamp symbols.
candidates.applies_because: The D arrangement is an open option for the R and S functions.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp and/or stop lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked 'Y', this is permitted for these functions; the reversing lamp function cannot be approved as 'Y'.
candidates.test_case: Check that a 'Y' marking, if used, appears only on the rear position and/or stop lamp symbols.
candidates.applies_because: The Y arrangement is an open option for the R and S functions.

candidates.text: A lamp approved as a rear position lamp is deemed to be also approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the approval documentation for the rear position lamp approval.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes an R148 rear position lamp.

candidates.text: A rear position lamp that is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with other functions may also be used as an end-outline marker lamp.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp configuration and approval documentation.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp is grouped with the stop and reversing lamps in one housing.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp using a common light source and is designed to operate permanently with an additional system regulating the intensity of the light emitted, this arrangement is permitted.
candidates.test_case: Review the circuit design and operating modes of the shared LEDs.
candidates.applies_because: Reciprocal incorporation of the R and S functions with shared LEDs is an open option.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources or (b) be intended for use on a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure of the lamps.
candidates.test_case: Verify the LED circuit design for multiple independent light sources, or the declared tell-tale dependence in the communication document.
candidates.applies_because: Reciprocal incorporation of the R and S functions is an open option for this lamp.

candidates.text: In case a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, only one logo is permitted, built into the internal optical structure or outer lens texture within the apparent surface, and all requirements of the rear position lamp function shall still be fulfilled.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the logo design and re-verify the rear position lamp photometry and colour with the logo present.
candidates.applies_because: Incorporating a vehicle manufacturer logo in the rear position lamp is an open option.

candidates.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, it shall be only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the logo and the vehicle manufacturer statement.
candidates.applies_because: The logo option is open for the rear position lamp.

candidates.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, the enclosed light-emitting surface of the logo (transparent and non-transparent components), in the direction of the reference axis, shall not exceed 100 cm2.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projected enclosed area of the logo in the reference axis direction.
candidates.applies_because: The logo option is open for the rear position lamp.

candidates.text: In case a logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, the logo light-emitting surface need not be symmetrical by itself, notwithstanding paragraph 5.5.2 of UN R48.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the left and right lamp logo designs.
candidates.applies_because: This relaxation applies to the logo option of the rear position lamp.

candidates.text: The stop lamp and reversing lamp functions shall not incorporate a logo.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the apparent surfaces of the stop and reversing lamps for any logo.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains stop and reversing lamp functions.

candidates.text: In a lamp function containing more than one light source, a group of LEDs wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.
candidates.test_case: Review the LED wiring schematic and identify the series strings treated as single light sources.
candidates.applies_because: The R, S and AR functions use multiple LEDs on a PCB.

candidates.text: In case the lamp relies on internal failure provisions only, upon failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp or stop lamp, the light intensity shall still comply with the minimum intensities of the pertinent standard light distribution in Annex 3, and with all light sources illuminated the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded.
candidates.test_case: Disable each light source (LED string) in turn and measure photometry against the minimum values; measure maxima with all sources lit.
candidates.applies_because: Internal failure provisions are an open option for the multi-LED R and S functions.

candidates.text: In case the lamp relies on a vehicle tell-tale, upon failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp or stop lamp, the lamp shall produce a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure as per UN R48 (e.g. paragraphs 6.7.8 and 6.10.8), and the lamp is then only for use on vehicles fitted with such a tell-tale.
candidates.test_case: Simulate failure of each light source and verify that the failure signal output is generated.
candidates.applies_because: Reliance on a vehicle tell-tale is an open option for failure detection.

candidates.text: In case of an R2 rear position lamp emitting more than the R1 maximum, upon failure of the variable intensity control the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
candidates.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure the intensities against the R1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The variable intensity R2 rear position lamp is an open option.

candidates.text: In case of an S2 stop lamp emitting more than the S1 maximum, upon failure of the variable intensity control the steady luminous intensity requirements of category S1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
candidates.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure the intensities against the S1 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The variable intensity S2 stop lamp is an open option.

candidates.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved under UN R37, R99 and/or R128 without use restriction, and/or light source modules, and/or non-replaceable light sources.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the light source design and documentation.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp uses LED light sources (non-replaceable, or modules).

candidates.text: The lamp shall not generate radiated or power-line disturbances that cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Perform radiated and conducted emission tests (e.g. per UN R10 ESA methods).
candidates.applies_because: The LED PCB with its driving circuitry is an electronic sub-assembly.

candidates.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall only be fittable in its designated and correct position.
candidates.test_case: Attempt to fit the module in incorrect positions and orientations.
candidates.applies_because: A replaceable LED module is an open light source option.

candidates.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
candidates.test_case: Attempt to remove the module by hand without tools.
candidates.applies_because: A replaceable LED module is an open light source option.

candidates.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall be tamperproof.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the module design for tamper resistance.
candidates.applies_because: A replaceable LED module is an open light source option.

candidates.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, each module shall, regardless of the use of tools, not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN-approved light source or with any other module of different characteristics in the same lamp housing.
candidates.test_case: Attempt to interchange the modules of the R, S and AR functions and to fit standard light sources.
candidates.applies_because: A replaceable LED module is an open light source option and the housing holds several functions.

candidates.text: In case of replaceable light source modules, when a module is replaced by another module from the applicant bearing the same identification code, the photometric requirements of the lamp shall be met.
candidates.test_case: Swap in a second module with the same MD code and repeat the photometric measurements.
candidates.applies_because: A replaceable LED module is an open light source option.

candidates.text: Photometric and colorimetric measurements of the lamp shall be made with its non-replaceable light sources or light source modules present in the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Conduct the photometric and colour tests on the complete lamp with its own LEDs.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp uses LED light sources fixed in the lamp.

candidates.text: In case the lamp may be installed in more than one position or in a field of positions, the photometric requirements shall be met for each position or for the extreme positions of the reference axis field specified by the manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements at each declared mounting position or extreme reference axis position.
candidates.applies_because: Installation positions of the rear lamp on M1 vehicles may vary.

candidates.text: Unless otherwise specified, the luminous intensities of the lamp functions shall be met with the light sources continuously lit.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensities with the functions continuously energised.
candidates.applies_because: The R, S and AR functions are steady-burning signal lamps.

candidates.text: An intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation is deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than 0.25° from that direction.
candidates.test_case: In case of a marginal result, evaluate intensities within ±0.25° of the test point.
candidates.applies_because: This tolerance applies to the photometric verification of each lamp function.

candidates.text: Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements when supplied at 13.5 V (12 V system), or 28 V in case of a 24 V system rating.
candidates.test_case: Supply the lamp at 13.5 V during the photometric and colour tests.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is intended for 12 V M1 vehicle systems.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Operate the lamp with the declared control gear and settings during the tests.
candidates.applies_because: Electronic control gear or variable intensity control is an open option.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control and uses non-replaceable light sources or light source modules, the lamp shall meet the requirements when operated as specified by the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Operate the lamp at the declared supply conditions during the tests.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp uses LED light sources, possibly without separate control gear.

candidates.text: The luminous intensity of each of the two samples on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the paragraph 5 table for each function (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp).
candidates.test_case: Measure the HV intensity of each function on two samples with a goniophotometer.
candidates.applies_because: The product has R, S and AR photometric functions.

candidates.text: The luminous intensity of each function shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the paragraph 5 table for that function.
candidates.test_case: Scan the full visible field of each function and compare the peak intensity with the maximum.
candidates.applies_because: The product has R, S and AR photometric functions.

candidates.text: Outside the reference axis, the luminous intensity of each function shall be not less than the minimum of the paragraph 5 table multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure (Figure A3-I for R and S), or not less than the cd value given in the figure (Figure A3-V for AR), for each direction.
candidates.test_case: Measure all grid points of Figure A3-I or A3-V and compare with the computed minima.
candidates.applies_because: The R, S and AR functions must meet a standard light distribution.

candidates.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Annex 2, the luminous intensity of each function shall be not less than the geometric visibility minimum specified in the paragraph 5 table.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity across the Annex 2 visibility field of each function.
candidates.applies_because: The R, S and AR functions have geometric visibility requirements.

candidates.text: The provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for each function.
candidates.test_case: Check intensities between grid points against the Annex 3 uniformity criteria.
candidates.applies_because: Annex 3 uniformity provisions apply to the R, S and AR light distributions.

candidates.text: In case of an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function, the assembly shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps are lit together.
candidates.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity with both lamps of the assembly lit.
candidates.applies_because: The D assembly is an open option for the R and S functions.

candidates.text: In case of an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' with the same function, the assembly shall comply with the minimum intensity requirement when either lamp has failed.
candidates.test_case: Measure the minimum intensities with each lamp of the assembly switched off in turn.
candidates.applies_because: The D assembly is an open option for the R and S functions.

candidates.text: In case of an interdependent lamp system ('Y'), the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
candidates.test_case: Measure photometry with all interdependent lamps of the system operated together.
candidates.applies_because: The interdependent system is an open option for the R and S functions.

candidates.text: In case an interdependent system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on a movable component (e.g. tailgate), the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component.
candidates.test_case: Measure the specified lamp(s) at each fixed position of the movable component.
candidates.applies_because: A split rear lamp on the M1 tailgate is a possible Y configuration.

candidates.text: In case an interdependent system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on a movable component, the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied if the specified interdependent lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values in the field of light distribution at all fixed positions of the movable component.
candidates.test_case: Verify the light distribution grid values at all fixed positions of the movable component.
candidates.applies_because: This relaxation applies to a split Y rear position lamp on a movable component.

candidates.text: In case of an R2 rear position lamp or S2 stop lamp, the variable intensity control shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
candidates.test_case: Drive the variable intensity control over its full range and measure the min/max intensities.
candidates.applies_because: Variable intensity R2/S2 operation is an open option.

candidates.text: In case of an R2 or S2 lamp with a variable intensity control depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, the control shall not cause intensities exceeding the steady (R1/S1) maximum under night-time conditions.
candidates.test_case: Set the control to night-time mode and measure the maximum intensities.
candidates.applies_because: Variable intensity R2/S2 operation is an open option.

candidates.text: In case of an R2 or S2 lamp with any other variable intensity control system, the control shall not cause intensities exceeding the steady (R1/S1) maximum under standard conditions (good visibility, MOR > 2,000 m, clean lens).
candidates.test_case: Set the control to the standard-conditions input and measure the maximum intensities.
candidates.applies_because: Variable intensity R2/S2 operation is an open option.

candidates.text: The luminous intensities of each function shall comply when tested according to Annex 8.
candidates.test_case: Run the Annex 8 photometric test sequence on the samples.
candidates.applies_because: The R, S and AR functions require photometric compliance testing.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by each function, measured inside the field of its light distribution grid in Annex 3, shall meet the colour prescribed for that function (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp).
candidates.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates across each function's light distribution grid with a spectroradiometer.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp emits red and white signal light through the PMMA lens.

candidates.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted shall be observed.
candidates.test_case: Visually and colorimetrically inspect the colour outside the grid field for abrupt changes.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to all signal functions of the lamp.

candidates.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp (R1 or R2) supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 4.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against all Table 4 values.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains a rear position lamp function of class R1 or R2.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, a luminous intensity of up to 60 cd is permitted for the rear position lamp below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
candidates.test_case: Measure rear position lamp intensity below 5°D and check it does not exceed 60 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamps may be reciprocally incorporated (open option).

candidates.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 or R2, the luminous intensity shall be at least 4 cd on the reference axis (HV), and outside the reference axis at least the product of 4 cd and the percentage of the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I for each direction.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at all Figure A3-I grid points and compare with the minimum values.
candidates.applies_because: The minimum and light distribution of Table 4 apply to both R1 and R2 rear position lamps.

candidates.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 17 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 17 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp may be category R1 (open option).

candidates.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 8.5 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 8.5 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be one of an assembly of two independent lamps marked D (open option).

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 42 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 42 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp may be category R2 (open option).

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 21 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 21 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be an R2 lamp marked D (open option).

candidates.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 for rear position lamps (R1, R2), the luminous intensity shall be at least 0.05 cd. These angles are 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally (20°/80° below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15°/5° for mounting height below 750 mm).
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity over the full geometric visibility field and verify ≥0.05 cd everywhere.
candidates.applies_because: Table 4 sets a minimum intensity within the geometric visibility angles for R1/R2 rear position lamps.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
candidates.test_case: Simulate single LED failures and a variable intensity control failure and check the intensity or the tell-tale signal per 4.6.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp contains multiple LED light sources and possibly a variable intensity control.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
candidates.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light and check against the red chromaticity limits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp has a rear position lamp function.

candidates.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the stop lamp (S1 or S2) supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 7.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against all Table 7 values.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains a stop lamp function of class S1 or S2.

candidates.text: For stop lamps of category S1 or S2, the luminous intensity shall be at least 60 cd on the reference axis (HV), and outside the reference axis at least the product of 60 cd and the percentage of the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I for each direction.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at all Figure A3-I grid points and compare with the minimum values.
candidates.applies_because: The minimum and light distribution of Table 7 apply to both S1 and S2 stop lamps.

candidates.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 260 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 260 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp may be category S1 (open option).

candidates.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 130 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan to find the maximum intensity and compare with 130 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be one of an assembly of two independent lamps marked D (open option).

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2) used as a single lamp, the luminous intensity shall not exceed 730 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 730 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp may be category S2 (open option).

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2) marked "D", the luminous intensity shall not exceed 365 cd in any direction in which the lamp is visible.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan at the highest intensity setting and compare the maximum with 365 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp may be an S2 lamp marked D (open option).

candidates.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1), the luminous intensity shall be at least 0.3 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1. These angles are 45° inboard / 45° outboard horizontally (20°/45° below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm) and 15° above / 15° below vertically (15°/5° for mounting height below 750 mm).
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity over the full geometric visibility field and verify ≥0.3 cd everywhere.
candidates.applies_because: Table 7 sets a minimum intensity within the geometric visibility angles for S1 stop lamps.

candidates.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2), the luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 shall be at least 0.3 cd under day conditions and at least 0.07 cd under night conditions. These angles are 45°/45° horizontally (20°/45° below the H-plane if mounted below 750 mm) and 15°/15° vertically (15°/5° if mounted below 750 mm).
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity over the geometric visibility field at the day and night intensity settings and compare with 0.3 cd and 0.07 cd.
candidates.applies_because: Table 7 sets day and night geometric visibility minima for S2 stop lamps.

candidates.text: The stop lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
candidates.test_case: Simulate single LED failures and a variable intensity control failure and check the intensity or the tell-tale signal per 4.6.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp contains multiple LED light sources and possibly a variable intensity control.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
candidates.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light and check against the red chromaticity limits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp has a stop lamp function.

candidates.text: The light emitted by each of the two samples of the reversing lamp (AR) supplied shall meet the requirements in Table 10.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples against all Table 10 values.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains a reversing lamp function of class AR.

candidates.text: In case the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices (reduced light distribution), the photometric intensity may be verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, where a luminous intensity of at least 25 cd shall be satisfied.
candidates.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity at 30° inwards and verify ≥25 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp may use the reduced light distribution for two-lamp fitment (open option).

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (AR), the luminous intensity shall be at least 80 cd on the reference axis (HV), and outside the reference axis at least the values derived from the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity at HV and at all Figure A3-V grid points and compare with the minimum values.
candidates.applies_because: Table 10 minimum and light distribution apply to the AR reversing lamp.

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (AR), the luminous intensity shall not exceed 300 cd in directions in or above the H-plane.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan in and above the H-plane and compare the maximum with 300 cd.
candidates.applies_because: Table 10 maximum applies to the AR reversing lamp.

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (AR), the luminous intensity shall not exceed 600 cd in directions below the H-plane down to 5°D.
