candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan between H and 5°D and compare the maximum with 600 cd.
candidates.applies_because: Table 10 maximum applies to the AR reversing lamp.

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (AR), the luminous intensity shall not exceed 8,000 cd in directions below 5°D.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric scan below 5°D and compare the maximum with 8,000 cd.
candidates.applies_because: Table 10 maximum applies to the AR reversing lamp.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
candidates.test_case: Simulate single LED failures and check the minimum intensity or the tell-tale signal per 4.6.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp uses multiple LED light sources.

candidates.text: The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
candidates.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reversing lamp light and check against the white chromaticity limits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp has a reversing lamp function behind a clear lens window.

candidates.text: Production lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) shall be manufactured so as to conform to the type approved under UN R148, including the specific technical requirements of paragraph 5.
candidates.test_case: Compare randomly selected production lamps with the approved type documentation and re-test them to paragraph 5 requirements.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp is type-approved under R148 and series production must match the approved type.

candidates.text: For production lamps, no measured photometric value of the rear position, stop or reversing lamp function shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148.
candidates.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of randomly selected production lamps per paragraph 4.8 and check that each value is within 20 per cent of the prescribed limits.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the permitted production deviation for the lamp's photometric performance.

candidates.text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields of Annexes 2 and 3, production lamps shall meet the equivalent values of Table 12. A required minimum of 7∙10^-1 cd corresponds to 5∙10^-1 cd (20 %) and 3∙10^-1 cd (30 %). 6∙10^-1 cd corresponds to 4∙10^-1 cd (20 %) and 2∙10^-1 cd (30 %). 3∙10^-1 cd corresponds to 2∙10^-1 cd (20 %) and 1∙10^-1 cd (30 %). 7∙10^-2 cd corresponds to 5∙10^-2 cd (20 %) and 3∙10^-2 cd (30 %). 5∙10^-2 cd corresponds to 3∙10^-2 cd (20 %) and 2∙10^-2 cd (30 %); this last row covers the minimum within the angles of geometric visibility for the R1/R2 and S1/S2 functions.
candidates.test_case: Measure the low-intensity points within the geometric visibility field of production samples and compare them with the Table 12 equivalent values.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamp functions have low minimum intensities (e.g. 0.05 cd within the geometric visibility angles), for which Table 12 sets the production equivalents.

candidates.text: Production lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates of their light colour when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9: red for the rear position and stop lamp functions, white for the reversing lamp.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function of randomly selected production lamps per paragraph 4.9 and check them against the colour boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: Conformity of production of the lamp covers its colorimetric characteristics.

candidates.text: Each lamp function (rear position lamp R1/R2 and stop lamp S1/S2) shall provide at least the minimum angles of geometric visibility, horizontal and vertical, given in Table A2-1 (Part A, Figures A2-I). The angles shown apply to a lamp mounted on the right side of the vehicle and are mirrored for a left-side lamp.
candidates.test_case: Goniometric check of the light-emitting surface visibility over the specified angular field for the right-hand and left-hand variants.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamp contains R148 rear position and stop lamp functions covered by Part A of Annex 2.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 80° outboard. For lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20° (20°/80°).
candidates.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface remains visible from 45° inboard to 80° outboard (20° inboard below H-plane if the mounting height is below 750 mm).
candidates.applies_because: P-01 is a rear position lamp of class R1 or R2.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below may be reduced to 5° (15°/5°).
candidates.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface remains visible from 15° up to 15° down (5° down if the mounting height is below 750 mm).
candidates.applies_because: P-01 is a rear position lamp of class R1 or R2.

candidates.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard and 45° outboard. For lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, the inboard angle below the H-plane may be reduced to 20° (20°/45°).
candidates.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the stop lamp apparent surface remains visible from 45° inboard to 45° outboard (20° inboard below H-plane if the mounting height is below 750 mm).
candidates.applies_because: P-02 is a stop lamp of class S1 or S2.

candidates.text: The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below may be reduced to 5° (15°/5°).
candidates.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the stop lamp apparent surface remains visible from 15° up to 15° down (5° down if the mounting height is below 750 mm).
candidates.applies_because: P-02 is a stop lamp of class S1 or S2.

candidates.text: Where the rear position lamp is also used as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1, RM2), it shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 0° inboard and 80° outboard.
candidates.test_case: Goniometric check of apparent surface visibility from 0° to 80° outboard.
candidates.applies_because: A rear position lamp approved under R148 is deemed approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp.

candidates.text: Where the rear position lamp is also used as a rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1, RM2), it shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above and 15° below the H-plane. For lamps to be installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the angle below may be reduced to 5° (15°/5°).
candidates.test_case: Goniometric check of apparent surface visibility from 15° up to 15° down (5° down if the mounting height is below 750 mm).
candidates.applies_because: A rear position lamp approved under R148 is deemed approved as a rear end-outline marker lamp.

candidates.text: For the rear position lamp (R1/R2), the stop lamp (S1/S2) and the reversing lamp, the minimum luminous intensities required in the various directions of measurement shall be the percentages shown in the applicable standard light distribution figure, applied to the minimum intensity required for the function. Each resulting value shall be mathematically rounded down to three significant digits. Directions are referenced to H = 0°, V = 0°, which is the reference axis through the centre of reference.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each grid point, compared with the figure percentage of the table minimum rounded down to three significant digits.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's rear position, stop and reversing functions are verified against the Annex 3 standard light distributions.

candidates.text: Where the rear position lamp (R1/R2) is intended to be installed at a mounting height of 750 mm or less above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), its photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Check the declared mounting height; if it is 750 mm or less, limit the downward photometric verification to V = 5° down.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp that may be mounted at 750 mm or less on an M1 car.

candidates.text: Where the stop lamp of category S1 or S2 is intended to be installed at a mounting height of 750 mm or less above the ground (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer), its photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Check the declared mounting height; if it is 750 mm or less, limit the downward photometric verification of the stop lamp to V = 5° down.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes an S1/S2 stop lamp that may be mounted at 750 mm or less on an M1 car.

candidates.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the luminous intensity of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall be at least the lowest minimum value (as a percentage) shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction.
candidates.test_case: Scan intermediate directions between the grid lines with a goniophotometer and confirm each value is at least the lowest surrounding grid minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamp functions have grid-type standard light distributions (Figure A3-I).

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp, if visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the beam; if local variations are seen, measure between adjacent measuring points and confirm each value is at least 50% of the lower prescribed minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp (AR).

candidates.text: In case of an R1 (steady) or an R2 (variable intensity) rear position lamp, the luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum luminous intensity required in Table 3.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the Figure A3-I percentages of the Table 3 minimum.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position lamp function, class R1 or R2, uses the Figure A3-I standard light distribution.

candidates.text: In case of an S1 (steady) or an S2 (variable intensity) stop lamp, the luminous intensity in each direction of measurement shall be at least the percentage given in Figure A3-I of the minimum luminous intensity required in Table 7, i.e. 60 cd.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points, compared with the Figure A3-I percentages of 60 cd.
candidates.applies_because: The stop lamp function, class S1 or S2, uses the Figure A3-I standard light distribution.

candidates.text: In case of a reversing lamp with standard light distribution, the luminous intensity at each measuring point of Figure A3-V (in degrees from the reference axis) shall be at least the minimum intensity in cd shown in Figure A3-V.
candidates.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each Figure A3-V measuring point, compared with the cd minima of Figure A3-V.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp (AR) that may have the standard light distribution.

candidates.text: From a mechanical and geometric standpoint, the differences of mass-produced rear combination lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions) from the approved type shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Inspect and measure dimensions and geometry of randomly selected production lamps and compare them with the approved type drawings and tolerances.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is an R148-approved lamp type whose series production must conform mechanically and geometrically to the approved type.

candidates.text: The photometric performance of any mass-produced lamp chosen at random (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions), tested according to paragraph 4.8 with the non-replaceable LED light sources or light source modules present in the lamp, shall meet the photometric requirements of this Regulation, so that the conformity of production is not contested.
candidates.test_case: Measure luminous intensities of a randomly selected production lamp per function at the Annex 3 grid points according to paragraph 4.8 and compare with the paragraph 5 values and the paragraph 6.1.3 deviation limits.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions of the product are subject to photometric conformity of production under R148.

candidates.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the light emitted by mass-produced lamps (red for the rear position and stop lamp functions, white for the reversing lamp function) shall be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function of a randomly selected production lamp within the light distribution grid per paragraph 4.9 and check them against the colour limits.
candidates.applies_because: The colour of the light emitted by each lamp function of the product is subject to colorimetric conformity of production under R148.

candidates.text: For the reversing lamp (non-incandescent, LED light sources), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp light distribution goniophotometrically after 1 min and after 10 min of operation and compare it with the minimum and maximum limits.
candidates.applies_because: The reversing lamp function uses LED light sources, not incandescent technology.

candidates.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp (non-incandescent, LED light sources), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure the rear position and stop lamp intensities after 1 min and after 30 min (or at photometric stability) and compare them with the minimum and maximum limits.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position and stop lamp functions are LED lamps other than reversing or manoeuvring lamps.

candidates.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function shall, in addition to paragraph 1 of Annex 8, comply at the point in time after switch-on listed in Table A8-1.
candidates.test_case: Check the intensity at the reference coordinate at the Table A8-1 time after switch-on, or show compliance via the LED provision of paragraph 2.1.2.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's rear position, stop and reversing functions are listed in Table A8-1.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements 4 seconds after switch ON (reference coordinate HV).
candidates.test_case: Record the HV intensity 4 s after switch-on and scale the distribution to check against the min/max limits.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a rear position lamp function.

candidates.text: The stop lamp shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements 0.2 seconds after switch ON (reference coordinate HV).
candidates.test_case: Record the HV intensity 0.2 s after switch-on with a fast photometer and check it against the min/max limits.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a stop lamp function.

candidates.text: The reversing lamp shall comply with its luminous intensity requirements 0.2 seconds after switch ON (reference coordinate HV).
candidates.test_case: Record the HV intensity 0.2 s after switch-on with a fast photometer and check it against the min/max limits.
candidates.applies_because: The product includes a reversing lamp function.

candidates.text: In case a lamp function uses LED technology only, the lamp function is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 of Annex 8 are compliant.
candidates.test_case: Confirm by inspection that each function uses LEDs only and that the measurements under paragraph 1.2 pass.
candidates.applies_because: All three lamp functions use LED light sources only.

candidates.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of each lamp function shall be met at all points in time, starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 (0.2 s for stop and reversing lamps, 4 s for the rear position lamp) and ending when photometric stability is reached.
candidates.test_case: Continuously record the HV intensity from the Table A8-1 time until photometric stability and verify that it never falls below the minimum.
candidates.applies_because: LED driver run-up behaviour of the lamp functions may raise doubt during approval testing.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall have a space large enough for either the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2, or the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the drawing and a sample to confirm there is a marking area large enough for the UI or the approval marking plus the other markings.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector (P-05) is a device of a type approved under R150.

candidates.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible and indelible.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the markings and rub them with water- and petrol-soaked cloths to check they stay legible.
candidates.applies_because: The R150 markings are applied to the retro-reflector or the combined lamp.

candidates.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value of 'a' defined in Table 1.
candidates.test_case: Measure the dimension 'a' of the approval marking on the sample.
candidates.applies_because: The approval marking on the Class IA/IB retro-reflector must be sized to Table 1.

candidates.text: For a retro-reflector for motor vehicles of Class IA (independent) or Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight), the minimum 'a' of the approval marking is 5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure 'a' on the approval mark and check it is at least 5 mm.
candidates.applies_because: The product's retro-reflector is Class IA or IB.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall contain the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter 'E', followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled 'E' and the country number.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector carries an R150 approval marking unless it is replaced by the UI.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall contain the four- to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the sequential number and check it against the approval communication.
candidates.applies_because: This is required content of the R150 approval marking on the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking to confirm the sequential number sits next to the circled E.
candidates.applies_because: This is a layout rule for the approval marking on the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: In case the lamp containing the retro-reflector is watertight, the approval marking shall contain the class symbol 'IA' (retro-reflector for motor vehicles, independent).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the symbol 'IA'.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: a watertight lamp makes the retro-reflector Class IA.

candidates.text: In case the lamp containing the retro-reflector is not watertight, the approval marking shall contain the class symbol 'IB' (retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for the symbol 'IB'.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: a non-watertight lamp makes the retro-reflector Class IB.

candidates.text: The approval marking shall contain the Regulation number '150', followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits of the series of amendments in force when the approval was issued (e.g. 150R01).
candidates.test_case: Inspect the marking for '150R' followed by the series digits.
candidates.applies_because: This is required content of the R150 approval marking on the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The approval marking may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available; in that case the UI mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I.
candidates.test_case: If a UI is used, compare the marked UI with the Figure I format and check the database entry.
candidates.applies_because: This is a marking option for the retro-reflector's R150 approval.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.
candidates.applies_because: This marking requirement applies to all R150 retro-reflective devices, including Class IA/IB.

candidates.text: A Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall bear the word 'TOP' written horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if this is needed to determine without ambiguity the angle(s) of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
candidates.test_case: Check whether the photometry depends on rotation and, if so, inspect for 'TOP' on the uppermost part of the illuminating surface.
candidates.applies_because: The product's retro-reflector is Class IA/IB and is non-triangular, so its orientation may matter.

candidates.text: The approval marking or Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4, shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the sample to confirm all markings are legible on the device.
candidates.applies_because: This sets where the R150 markings are located on the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Where the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (rear position, stop and reversing lamps with the retro-reflector) comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four- to six-digit sequential number, or a single Unique Identifier, may be affixed anywhere on the lamp assembly, subject to the conditions of paragraphs 3.3.6.1.1 and 3.3.6.1.2.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the single mark on the assembly and check that it covers all applicable approvals.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is integrated in a rear combination lamp also approved under R148.

candidates.text: If a single approval mark or UI is used on the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps, it shall be visible after the lamp is installed on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed on the vehicle, or a mock-up, to confirm the mark is visible.
candidates.applies_because: This is a condition for using a single mark on the rear combination lamp.

candidates.text: If a single approval mark or UI is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped/combined/reciprocally incorporated lamps (e.g. the outer lens or the retro-reflector) shall be removable without also removing the approval mark with its sequential number or the UI.
candidates.test_case: Review the design and do a disassembly check that the mark sits on a part that cannot be separated from the light-transmitting parts.
candidates.applies_because: This is a condition for using a single mark on the rear combination lamp.

candidates.text: The components of a single approval mark shall be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval was granted (R150, R148).
candidates.test_case: Measure the mark components and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R150 and R148.
candidates.applies_because: This applies if the combined lamp uses a single approval mark.

candidates.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications', and of the Annexes they reference, in UN Regulation No. 48 (series of amendments in force at the time of application) shall apply to the retro-reflector. This covers those pertinent to the retro-reflector and to the M1 vehicle category on which it is intended to be installed, where verification at device type approval is feasible.
candidates.test_case: Review the R48 general and individual specifications for rear retro-reflectors on M1 vehicles and check those verifiable at device level.
candidates.applies_because: The red rear retro-reflector is intended for installation on M1 vehicles under UN R48.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and continues to do so in normal use.
candidates.test_case: Verify retained photometric and colorimetric compliance after the prescribed resistance tests (heat, water, corrosion, fuel).
candidates.applies_because: This general construction requirement applies to all retro-reflective devices, including the integral Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector must not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the samples and review the design for defects affecting operation or maintenance.
candidates.applies_because: This general construction requirement applies to all retro-reflective devices, including the integral Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The components of the retro-reflector, or parts thereof, shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
candidates.test_case: Attempt manual disassembly of the retro-reflector components without tools and confirm they cannot easily be separated.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to the retro-reflector insert and its attachment within the rear lamp.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the outer surface and confirm it can be cleaned easily.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to the exposed outer surface of the retro-reflector or the lens covering it.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough, and any protuberances it may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the outer surface visually and by touch for roughness and for protuberances that hinder cleaning.
candidates.applies_because: This applies to the exposed outer surface of the retro-reflector or the lens covering it.

candidates.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the mounted lamp assembly and confirm the inner (prism) surface cannot be reached in normal use.
candidates.applies_because: The product contains a retro-reflector, whose prism inner surface must be enclosed.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter (e.g. a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter), the optical unit and filter must be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the assembly and attempt separation of the optical unit and filter under normal use conditions; confirm they cannot be separated.
candidates.applies_because: An open option is a colourless optical unit behind the red PMMA outer lens acting as a filter.

candidates.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
candidates.test_case: Inspect and review the material specification to confirm the red colour is from the material (mass-tinted), not paint or varnish.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is red, so its colour must come from tinted material, not from coating.

candidates.text: When the retro-reflector is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the UN R48 limits for red night-time retro-reflected light. If 0° produces a colourless surface reflection, the angle β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° of Annex 4 Part 1 paragraph 1.1 shall be used.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light under Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and 0°/0° (or -5°/0°) illumination, and compare with the R48 red limits.
candidates.applies_because: The rear retro-reflector is red, and night-time colour limits apply to red retro-reflective devices.

candidates.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the dimension and shape requirements of Annex 5.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the shape and dimensions of the retro-reflector against Annex 5, paragraph 1.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red non-triangular retro-reflector (P-05) is approved as Class IA or IB.

candidates.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5.
candidates.test_case: Perform goniophotometric RI and night-time colour measurements per Annex 4 Part 1 and paragraph 4.2.1.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a Class IA/IB retro-reflector subject to the RI and colour limits.

candidates.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements that apply to the nature of its materials and construction.
candidates.test_case: Run the heat, water, fuel/oil, corrosion, rear-face, stability and weathering tests applicable to the construction.
candidates.applies_because: The moulded PMMA retro-reflector must pass the resistance tests for its material and construction.

candidates.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape of trailer retro-reflectors when observed from a distance of 10 m.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the retro-reflector from 10 m and confirm it does not look triangular.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a non-triangular Class IA/IB rear retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, then 1 h cooling at 23 °C ± 2 °C). At least one hour after this test it shall meet the colour requirements of paragraph 5.1.5 and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4 at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the position defined in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2).
candidates.test_case: Condition the samples for 48 h at 65 °C, cool for 1 h, then measure colour and RI at 20' and 0°/0°.
candidates.applies_because: The heat test is the first test for all moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflectors.

candidates.text: After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflector, and in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the samples for cracks and distortion after the 48 h / 65 °C exposure.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a moulded plastics (PMMA) Class IA/IB reflector subject to the heat test.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector, as part of the lamp and stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 min in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the top of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. This is repeated with the device turned through 180° so that the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water, followed immediately by immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
candidates.test_case: Immerse the lamp and retro-reflector as specified, then inspect for water and measure RI.
candidates.applies_because: Water penetration is the first-group test for Class IA/IB retro-reflectors, including those that are part of a lamp.

candidates.text: After the water penetration test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. Where visual inspection does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the RI shall still satisfy paragraph 5.1.4 at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the prism surface for water and, in case of doubt, re-measure RI at 20' and 0°/0°.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the water penetration test for P-05.

candidates.text: After a satisfactory water penetration test, the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the tests for resistance to motor fuels and lubricating oils (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7; 5 min exposure each).
candidates.test_case: Expose the outer surface to the n-heptane/toluol mixture and then to detergent lubricating oil for 5 min each, then inspect and measure colour and RI.
candidates.applies_because: The first test group for Class IA/IB retro-reflectors includes resistance to fuels and lubricants.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, it shall be subjected to the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 h exposure, 2 h interval, 24 h exposure).
candidates.test_case: Perform the salt-spray corrosion test per Annex 6 Part 4, then inspect and measure colour and RI.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the retro-reflector may contain essential metal components susceptible to corrosion.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is mirror-backed with an accessible rear face, it shall be subjected to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face in Part 5 of Annex 6.
candidates.test_case: Brush the rear face and apply the fuel mixture per Annex 6 Part 5, then measure RI.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: the prisms may be metallised (mirror-backed) with an accessible rear face.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of its optical properties in Part 3 of Annex 4.
candidates.test_case: Check colour and RI of samples after the stability-in-time assessment per Annex 4 Part 3.
candidates.applies_because: The third test group for Class IA/IB retro-reflectors covers stability in time.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test of Part 6 of Annex 6 (accelerated artificial weathering per EN ISO 4892-2:2013).
candidates.test_case: Expose the samples in a xenon-arc weathering chamber per EN ISO 4892-2:2013, then measure colour and RI.
candidates.applies_because: The fourth test group for Class IA/IB retro-reflectors covers weathering.

candidates.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each test group shall have a colour that satisfies paragraph 5.1.5 (red night-time colour per UN R48).
candidates.test_case: Check colour visually after each test group and measure trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt.
candidates.applies_because: This is the colour pass criterion after the resistance tests for P-05.

candidates.text: After undergoing the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each test group shall have an RI satisfying paragraph 5.1.4. Verification is at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° only, or if necessary in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: Measure RI at 20' and 0°/0° after each test group and compare with Table 3 (red: ≥ 300 mcd/lx).
candidates.applies_because: This is the photometric pass criterion after the resistance tests for P-05.

candidates.text: For photometric measurements, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the retro-reflector's optical system, as indicated by the manufacturer, shall be considered. This surface shall lie within a circle of 200 mm diameter and be limited to 100 cm², although the retro-reflecting optical units need not attain this area.
candidates.test_case: Check on the drawing and sample that the declared illuminating surface lies within a 200 mm circle and is ≤ 100 cm².
candidates.applies_because: This defines the measured illuminating surface of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, in mcd/lx, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
candidates.test_case: Perform goniophotometric RI measurements at all Table 3 angles for red Class IA/IB.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a red Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Minimum RI for red Class IA/IB retro-reflectors: at divergence 20', 300 mcd/lx at β1 = 0°/β2 = 0°, 200 mcd/lx at β1 = ±10°/β2 = 0°, and 100 mcd/lx at β1 = ±5°/β2 = ±20°. At divergence 1°30', 5 mcd/lx at 0°/0°, 2.8 mcd/lx at ±10°/0°, and 2.5 mcd/lx at ±5°/±20°.
candidates.test_case: Measure RI at each listed angle combination and compare with the minima.
candidates.applies_because: These are the Table 3 values for the red Class IA/IB row that applies to P-05.

candidates.text: The RI of the retro-reflector shall not be lower than the values specified for the outer illumination angles within the solid angle that has the centre of reference as its apex and is bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
candidates.test_case: Scan RI within the bounded solid angle and confirm no value falls below the outer-angle minima.
candidates.applies_because: This limits RI inside the measuring solid angle for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: Where the Class IA/IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane less than 750 mm above the ground, its RI values may be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
candidates.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and, if below 750 mm, limit downward RI verification to 5°.
candidates.applies_because: The rear lamp of an M1 car may be mounted with the retro-reflector below 750 mm.

candidates.text: If the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° and a divergence of 20' it shall be rotated about its axis of reference to the position of minimum RI, and that minimum RI shall conform to the value of paragraph 5. If the specified values are not attained at other angles in this position, the device may be rotated ±5° from it.
candidates.test_case: Rotate the sample about its reference axis, find the minimum RI at 20' and 0°/0°, and verify compliance.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is photometrically assessed in this position unless it is marked TOP.

candidates.text: The night-time colour of the retro-reflector shall be tested by the method of paragraph 4.2.1: CIE Standard Illuminant A, angle of divergence 1/3°, illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the Annex 4 Part 1, paragraph 1.1 angle if a colourless surface reflection occurs).
candidates.test_case: Measure chromaticity of the retro-reflected light under Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the colour measurement conditions for the red retro-reflector P-05.

candidates.text: The trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red specified in UN Regulation No. 48. This applies both in case of a red-coloured optical unit and in case of a colourless optical unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter.
candidates.test_case: Measure the x,y chromaticity of the reflected light and compare with the UN R48 red night-time colour boundaries.
candidates.applies_because: P-05 is a red rear retro-reflector; the open option of a red optical unit or a red filter lens does not change the limit.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors (Class IA/IB, red) shall conform mechanically and geometrically to the approved type; differences shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure shape and dimensions of production retro-reflectors and compare them with the approved type drawings and the Annex 5 Class IA/IB limits.
candidates.applies_because: The integral rear retro-reflector P-05 is approved under R150 and must be produced in conformity with the approved type.

candidates.text: For photometric performance of any mass-produced retro-reflector chosen at random, no measured value (coefficient of luminous intensity) shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
candidates.test_case: Measure the CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors at the prescribed angles and check that each value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the permitted photometric deviation of production retro-reflectors of the rear lamp.

candidates.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates prescribed for red retro-reflected light.
candidates.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production samples per the colorimetric test conditions and check that they lie within the red limits.
candidates.applies_because: The red rear retro-reflector must keep its approved colour in series production.

candidates.text: When the RI of the red retro-reflector (Class IA/IB) is measured at β1 = β2 = 0° and a mirror effect is produced on slightly turning the device, the RI reading shall be taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° and shall meet the prescribed value there.
candidates.test_case: Turn the sample slightly on the goniometer at β1 = β2 = 0° to check for specular reflection; if present, measure RI at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° and compare with the limit.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the illumination angle at which the retro-reflector's RI is verified if its front surface gives a mirror reflection.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and an angle of divergence of 20', the minimum RI found on rotating the retro-reflector about its axis of reference shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5 (for red Class IA/IB: at least 300 mcd/lx).
candidates.test_case: Rotate the unmarked sample through 360° about its reference axis at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, find the minimum RI and verify it is at least 300 mcd/lx.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector may be unmarked for orientation, so its RI is checked at the worst rotation position.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", the RI at the other angles of illumination and divergence shall be met with the device in the rotation position ε of minimum RI. If the specified values are not attained there, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference by up to ±5° from that position.
candidates.test_case: Perform the complete photometry at the minimum-RI rotation position and, where a value fails, re-measure within ±5° rotation to check compliance.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the rotation position, with its permitted ±5° tolerance, at which the unmarked retro-reflector must meet the full photometric table.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector is marked "TOP", at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified) and an angle of divergence of 20', the RI shall not fall below the prescribed value (for red Class IA/IB: 300 mcd/lx) in any position assumed during rotation of the device by ±5° about its axis of reference.
candidates.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked sample ±5° about its reference axis at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, record RI continuously and check it stays at least 300 mcd/lx.
candidates.applies_because: This is a design option: if the retro-reflector carries a TOP mark, its RI must hold over ±5° rotation.

candidates.text: If, at β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0°, the RI of the retro-reflector exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, the RI requirements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be met at ε = 0°.
candidates.test_case: Measure RI at ε = 0° and β1 = β2 = 0°; if it is at least 150 % of the limit, perform all photometric measurements at ε = 0° and compare with Table 3.
candidates.applies_because: This sets the rotation position at which the retro-reflector's full photometric compliance is assessed when it has a high RI margin.

candidates.text: The retro-reflection (RI) of the retro-reflector shall meet its requirements when illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
candidates.test_case: Verify that the photometric test uses a source calibrated to CIE Standard Illuminant A (2856 K) and check RI results against the limits.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the illuminant under which the retro-reflector's photometric performance is verified.

candidates.text: The shape of the illuminating surfaces of the Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors of Classes IIIA and IIIB (paragraph 2.1.) when observed from a distance of 10 metres.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector from 10 m and confirm its shape cannot be mistaken for a triangle.
candidates.applies_because: The integral non-triangular red retro-reflector of the rear lamp is a Class IA or IB device under R150.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector (Class IA, or Class IB where the moisture and dust alternative is not used), whether part of the rear lamp or not and stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C. The test is done first with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface. It is then repeated with the device turned through 180°, so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water.
candidates.test_case: Immerse the stripped retro-reflector or lamp unit in a 50 °C ± 5 °C water bath for 10 min in each of the two orientations at the prescribed depths.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector of the rear lamp is a Class IA/IB retro-reflector that must resist water penetration.

candidates.text: Immediately after the 50 °C immersions, the retro-reflector shall withstand immersion under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.
candidates.test_case: Transfer the sample immediately to a 25 °C ± 5 °C water bath and repeat the immersions under the same conditions.
candidates.applies_because: The water penetration exposure of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector includes the subsequent 25 °C immersion.

candidates.text: After the water immersion test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. If visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall be considered to have failed the test.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the reflecting surface of the retro-reflector for water after the immersion sequence.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the water penetration test for the Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water, or in case of doubt, the retro-reflector shall still meet the CIL (RI) requirements of paragraph 5.1.4 after the water immersion test. The RI is measured by the method of paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions of Part 1 of Annex 4. The device is first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
candidates.test_case: Lightly shake the sample, then measure the CIL at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector of the rear lamp must keep its photometric performance after the water penetration test.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB (not watertight lamp) where the manufacturer requests the moisture and dust test alternative, the retro-reflector (as part of the lamp) shall be exposed to a solid-cone water spray. The spray shall be directed downward at 45° ± 5° to the vertical, with a precipitation rate at the device of 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, while the device rotates about its vertical axis at 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
candidates.test_case: Run the water spray cabinet test with the verified precipitation rate, nozzle angle and rotation speed on a lamp sample.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: if the lamp housing is not watertight, the retro-reflector is Class IB and this moisture test may replace the water penetration test.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test alternative, the rear position, stop and reversing functions grouped or reciprocally incorporated with the retro-reflector shall be operated at design voltage during the water spray, in a cycle of 5 min ON and 55 min OFF.
candidates.test_case: Energise the lamp functions at design voltage with a 5 min ON / 55 min OFF timer during the spray test.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is integrated in a rear combination lamp with signalling and lighting functions.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test alternative, the water spray exposure shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min), followed by a 1 h drain period with rotation and spray off.
candidates.test_case: Record the spray duration and the drain period during the test.
candidates.applies_because: This is the duration of the moisture exposure the Class IB device must withstand.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test alternative, the lamp shall be tested with all drain holes and other openings open, and any drain wicks used shall be fitted in the device during the test.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the sample before the test to confirm that openings are open and drain wicks are fitted.
candidates.applies_because: Drain holes and wicks in the lamp design are part of the tested configuration.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test alternative, after the drain period no standing pool of water shall have formed in the interior of the device, nor be formable by tapping or tilting the device.
candidates.test_case: After the 1 h drain period, inspect the lamp interior visually and tap and tilt it to check for pooled water.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the moisture test for a non-watertight retro-reflector housing.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the moisture test alternative, the retro-reflector shall be photometrically evaluated after the moisture test. Its RI shall be measured according to Part 1 of Annex 4 after the exterior has been dried.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI before and after the spray test on a goniophotometer per Annex 4 Part 1 and compare with the required values.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector must keep its photometric performance after moisture exposure.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the dust test alternative, the retro-reflector (in the lamp) shall be exposed to fine powdered cement test dust (ASTM C 150-84) in a dust chamber for 5 hours. The dust shall be agitated every 15 min for 2 to 15 s and allowed to settle between agitations.
candidates.test_case: Run the dust chamber exposure with cement dust per ASTM C 150-84 for 5 h at the prescribed agitation intervals.
candidates.applies_because: Open option: a non-watertight Class IB retro-reflector may be tested for dust penetration instead of water penetration.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the dust test alternative, the lamp shall be dust-tested with all drain holes and other openings open, and any drain wicks used shall be fitted in the device.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the sample configuration before the dust exposure.
candidates.applies_because: Openings in the lamp design form part of the dust-tested configuration.

candidates.text: In case of Class IB with the dust test alternative, after the dust exposure and cleaning of the exterior, the retro-reflector RI shall satisfy paragraph 5.1.4. It is measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 at a divergence angle of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1 paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 if necessary.
candidates.test_case: Measure the RI at 20' / 0° after the dust exposure and compare with the paragraph 5.1.4 requirements.
candidates.applies_because: Dust penetration must not significantly degrade the photometric output of the retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall be designed so that it retains the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which it is normally exposed.
candidates.test_case: After the saline-mist corrosion test, re-measure the photometric and colorimetric values and compare them with the prescribed limits.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red Class IA/IB retro-reflector of the rear lamp is a retro-reflective device under R150.

candidates.text: The front surface of the retro-reflector shall resist tarnishing and the protection of its rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly where an essential metal component is liable to be attacked, when tested for corrosion resistance according to ISO 9227:2017.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the front surface and the rear-face protection for tarnishing or deterioration after the ISO 9227 salt-spray exposure.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is exposed to humidity and corrosion at the rear exterior of the vehicle and may carry metallised (mirror-backed) prisms.

candidates.text: The retro-reflector shall withstand exposure to a saline mist for a period of 50 hours. Because it is combined with a lamp, the complete rear lamp is tested, stripped of all removable parts. The 50 hours comprise two 24-hour exposure periods separated by a 2-hour interval during which the sample dries.
candidates.test_case: Expose the lamp, stripped of removable parts, to salt mist for 2 × 24 h with a 2 h drying interval, then evaluate it.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is integrated in the rear combination lamp, so the lamp is the test sample.

candidates.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion (e.g. metallised mirror-backed prisms), the device shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
candidates.test_case: Run the salt-mist exposure with a 5 % NaCl solution at 35 ± 2 °C and verify the chamber settings.
candidates.applies_because: It is an open option whether the retro-reflector contains essential metal components susceptible to corrosion.

candidates.text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflector shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the sample immediately after the salt-mist test for corrosion that could impair its efficiency.
candidates.applies_because: This is the pass criterion of the corrosion test that the retro-reflector must undergo.

candidates.text: After a 48-hour recovery period following the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively. RA is measured as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6 at an entrance angle β2 = 5° and an observation angle α = 20'.
candidates.test_case: After 48 h recovery and removal of salt deposits, measure the retro-reflection at β2 = 5° and α = 20' and compare it with the referenced limits.
candidates.applies_because: This photometric pass criterion after the corrosion test applies to retro-reflective areas, which include the retro-reflector's prism area.

candidates.text: In case of a mirror-backed (metallised) moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflector with an accessible rear face, the rear face shall withstand the following sequence: brushing with a hard nylon brush, then application for one minute of a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture of Annex 7 Part 1 (70 vol. % n-heptane and 30 vol. % toluol), then brushing again with the same brush once evaporation is complete.
candidates.test_case: Brush the rear face with a hard nylon brush, apply a cloth soaked in 70/30 n-heptane/toluol for 1 min, let it dry and brush again, then proceed to the RI measurement.
candidates.applies_because: The retro-reflector is a moulded PMMA Class IA/IB device, and the open option of a mirror-backed rear face makes this rear-face resistance test applicable.

candidates.text: In case of a mirror-backed Class IA/IB retro-reflector with an accessible rear face, after the rear-face resistance test and with the whole mirror-backed rear face covered with Indian ink, the coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) shall still satisfy the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4. The check is made per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or, if necessary, in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1 paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: Cover the tested rear face completely with Indian ink and measure the RI goniometrically at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, then compare it with the paragraph 5.1.4 limits for red Class IA/IB.
candidates.applies_because: The pass criterion of the rear-face resistance test binds the mirror-backed option of the product's Class IA/IB retro-reflector.

candidates.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector, in particular its illuminating surface, shall withstand exposure to a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol applied by light wiping with a soaked cotton cloth (resistance to fuels test).
candidates.test_case: Lightly wipe the outer and illuminating surface of the retro-reflector with a cotton cloth soaked in 70/30 n-heptane/toluol mixture.
candidates.applies_because: The integral Class IA/IB retro-reflector of the rear lamp is a retro-reflective device subject to the fuel resistance test.

candidates.text: About five minutes after application of the n-heptane/toluol test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflector shall show no apparent surface changes on visual inspection, except that slight surface cracks are not objected to.
candidates.test_case: Visually inspect the wiped surface of the retro-reflector about 5 minutes after wiping for surface changes other than slight cracks.
candidates.applies_because: This pass criterion applies to the retro-reflector integrated in the rear lamp.

candidates.text: After the outer surface of the moulded plastics Class IA/IB retro-reflector, in particular its illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes, its CIL (RI) shall still meet the conditions of paragraph 5.1.4. This is verified at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0°, or, if necessary, in all positions of Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
candidates.test_case: Wipe the illuminating surface with detergent lubricating oil and clean it after 5 min. Then measure the CIL at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0° and compare it with the 5.1.4 limits.
candidates.applies_because: The integral red retro-reflector is a moulded PMMA Class IA/IB reflector, so the lubricating oil resistance test applies.

candidates.text: The external projection provisions do not apply to those parts of the rear lamp's external surface (lens, visible housing rim, exposed seal) which, with the vehicle laden and all doors, windows and access lids closed, are at a height of more than 2 m.
candidates.test_case: Measure the height of the lamp's exposed surfaces on the laden vehicle with all closures shut.
candidates.applies_because: Exemption that applies to any lamp surface mounted above 2 m on the M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: The external projection provisions do not apply to those parts of the rear lamp's external surface which, with the vehicle laden and all doors, windows and access lids closed, are below the floor line.
candidates.test_case: Determine the floor line on the laden vehicle and check which lamp surfaces lie below it.
candidates.applies_because: Exemption that applies to any portion of the installed lamp lying below the floor line.

candidates.text: The external projection provisions do not apply to those parts of the rear lamp's external surface (e.g. recessed lens or housing edges, a concealed seal) which, with the vehicle laden and all closures shut, cannot be contacted by a 100 mm diameter sphere, both in their static condition and in operation.
candidates.test_case: Apply a 100 mm diameter sphere to the lamp area on the vehicle and identify the surfaces it cannot contact.
candidates.applies_because: Exemption that applies to recessed or concealed edges of the lamp installed in the body.

candidates.text: The external surface formed by the installed rear lamp shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by or brushing against it in a collision.
candidates.test_case: Visually and tactilely inspect the installed lamp's lens, rim and seal for pointed, sharp or injurious projections.
candidates.applies_because: Lighting and light-signalling devices form part of the M1 vehicle's external surface.

candidates.text: The external surface formed by the installed rear lamp shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the installed lamp and its junction with the body for outward-directed hooks, edges or gaps that could catch.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's exposed surfaces are part of the vehicle's external surface.

candidates.text: In case the rear lamp (lens or housing rim/bezel) protrudes 5 mm or more beyond the panel, no protruding part of it shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projection per Annex 3 para 2 and check the edge radii with radius gauges.
candidates.applies_because: Applies if the lamp protrudes beyond the body panel nominal line (open option).

candidates.text: In case parts of the rear lamp's external surface protrude less than 5 mm but 1.5 mm or more, the 2.5 mm minimum radius does not apply, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projection of the edges per Annex 3 and inspect the outward facing angles for blunting.
candidates.applies_because: Applies to a lamp that is nearly flush, or to lens or rim edges with small protrusion and radius < 2.5 mm (open option).

candidates.text: Parts of the rear lamp's external surface which protrude less than 1.5 mm are exempt from both the 2.5 mm minimum radius and the blunting requirement.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projection per Annex 3 para 2 and confirm it is below 1.5 mm.
candidates.applies_because: Relaxation that applies to a flush-mounted lamp, or to edges that barely protrude (open option).

candidates.text: Protruding parts of the rear lamp's external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A (e.g. an exposed TPE/silicone seal) may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm.
candidates.test_case: Measure the Shore A hardness of the exposed seal on the installed lamp and check its edge radii.
candidates.applies_because: Applies if the gasket is visible at the external surface and has a radius below 2.5 mm (open option).

candidates.text: When the hardness exemption is claimed, the hardness of the rear lamp part shall be measured with the component as installed on the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Perform the Shore A durometer measurement on the part while it is mounted on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: Applies to an exposed soft seal or other low-hardness lamp part relying on the hardness exemption.

candidates.text: Where a Shore A hardness measurement of the rear lamp part is impossible, comparable measurements shall be used to evaluate it against the 60 Shore A threshold.
candidates.test_case: Document and perform an equivalent hardness measurement method and compare the result against the 60 Shore A equivalent.
candidates.applies_because: Applies when the exposed lamp part cannot be measured by the Shore A procedure.

candidates.text: Vehicles approved under UN R26 shall be manufactured to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 5 and 6. For the rear combination lamp, this means the exposed outer lens, any visible housing rim and any exposed seal on series-production vehicles must keep the approved external-projection characteristics: no pointed or sharp parts, radius of curvature of at least 2.5 mm, or the hardness of 60 Shore A or less or the small-projection exemptions where they are used.
candidates.test_case: On production samples of the lamp as installed, measure edge radii, projection heights (Annex 3 method) and Shore A hardness, and compare them with the approved type and the limits of paragraph 5.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp's exposed surfaces form part of the M1 vehicle's external surface, which must stay compliant with paragraph 5 throughout production.

candidates.text: In case the rear lamp protrudes beyond the panel nominal line and is mounted on a convex surface, the dimension of the projection of the rear lamp may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the lamp in its installed condition.
candidates.test_case: Measure the lamp's projection directly on the installed vehicle, or check it on the manufacturer's installed-condition section drawing.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is a component mounted on the vehicle's external surface, and its projection is assessed against R26 para 5/6 limits.

candidates.text: In case the rear lamp protrudes beyond the panel nominal line and is mounted on a surface other than convex, and its projection cannot be determined by simple measurement, the dimension of the projection of the lamp shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over the lamp in constant contact with it.
candidates.test_case: Move a 100 mm sphere over the installed lamp in constant contact and record the maximum variation of the sphere-centre distance from the panel nominal line.
candidates.applies_because: This method defines how the projection of the installed lamp is measured for the R26 projection limits.

candidates.text: The rear combination lamp (rear position, stop, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector) shall be so fitted that, under normal conditions of use and notwithstanding any vibrations to which it may be subjected, it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R48 and enables the vehicle to comply with the requirements of UN R48.
candidates.test_case: Vibration test of the lamp on its mounting, then re-measure photometry, colour and orientation against R48 values.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp is a light-signalling device installed on an M1 vehicle.

candidates.text: It shall not be possible for the rear combination lamp to be inadvertently maladjusted.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the mounting design and check that the reference axis does not shift after the vibration and handling checks.
candidates.applies_because: The fasteners and housing fix the lamp's aim on the vehicle.

candidates.text: The reference axis of each signalling function of the lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the vertical angle of the lamp reference axis relative to the road plane on the installed vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector are light-signalling devices.

candidates.text: The reference axis of each signalling function of the lamp, when fitted to the vehicle, shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
candidates.test_case: Measure the horizontal angle of the lamp reference axis relative to the vehicle median longitudinal plane.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp functions are signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors or side-marker lamps.

candidates.text: Any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the lamp manufacturer shall be complied with when the lamp is installed.
candidates.test_case: Compare the installation against the manufacturer's fitting instructions.
candidates.applies_because: Fitting instructions for the lamp govern its installed orientation.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamp shall be verified with the vehicle unladen, on a flat horizontal surface, in normal condition of use (propulsion system running, movable components in normal position).
candidates.test_case: Measure lamp height and orientation with the unladen vehicle on a flat horizontal surface with the engine running.
candidates.applies_because: This defines the vehicle condition under which the lamp's installed position and orientation are assessed.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the left and right lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Measure the lateral positions of the exterior outlines of the left and right lamps relative to the vehicle centre plane.
candidates.applies_because: The rear combination lamps are fitted as a left/right pair.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane, except for the interior structure of the lamp.
candidates.test_case: Compare the exterior geometry of the left and right lamps for mirror symmetry.
candidates.applies_because: The left and right lamps form a pair.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
candidates.test_case: Measure chromaticity of each function on the left and right lamps.
candidates.applies_because: Each paired function (position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector) must match in colour.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics.
candidates.test_case: Compare the photometric distributions of each function in the left and right lamps.
candidates.applies_because: The left and right lamps form a pair.

candidates.text: In case the lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo may be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and only vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are permitted.
candidates.test_case: Inspect the vehicle rear for the number, position and ownership of illuminated logos.
candidates.applies_because: A logo in the lens or light-emitting surface is an open option for the lamp.

candidates.text: On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the pair requirements of paragraph 5.5 shall be satisfied as far as is possible.
candidates.test_case: Review the asymmetry justification and check symmetry wherever the body shape permits.
candidates.applies_because: This relaxation applies to the paired lamp if the vehicle rear is asymmetrical.

candidates.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and rear retro-reflector may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another, provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.
candidates.test_case: Verify each function individually for colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility and electrical connection on the vehicle.
candidates.applies_because: The product integrates several functions in a common lamp body.

candidates.text: The photometric and colorimetric requirements of each lamp function shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.
candidates.test_case: Measure photometry and chromaticity of each function with all other functions switched OFF.
candidates.applies_because: The functions are grouped or reciprocally incorporated in one lamp.

candidates.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp (or another function that can be switched ON together with it), the colour requirements of that other function shall be fulfilled when both the reciprocally incorporated function and the rear position lamp are switched ON.
candidates.test_case: Measure stop lamp chromaticity with the rear position lamp and stop lamp switched ON simultaneously.
candidates.applies_because: Reciprocal incorporation of the rear position and stop lamps is an open option.

candidates.text: In case a single lamp function (other than the retro-reflector) has an apparent surface composed of two or more distinct parts, either the total projected area of the distinct parts in the direction of the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the minimum distance between facing edges of adjacent distinct parts shall not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.
candidates.test_case: Determine the projected apparent surface parts and compute the area ratio or measure the gap between adjacent parts.
candidates.applies_because: The LED reflector-cell layout may split a function's apparent surface into distinct parts.

candidates.text: In case a function is obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D", either the projection of the apparent surfaces of the two lamps in the direction of the reference axis shall occupy not less than 60 per cent of the smallest circumscribing quadrilateral, or the minimum distance between the facing edges of the two apparent surfaces shall not exceed 75 mm measured perpendicular to the reference axis.
candidates.test_case: Measure the projected apparent surfaces of both D lamps and compute the area ratio or the edge gap.
candidates.applies_because: Being part of a 'D' lamp assembly is an open option for the lamp.

candidates.text: In case the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked "Y", the system shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1; two or more lamps or separate apparent surfaces within the same lamp body or behind a common outer lens shall not be considered an interdependent lamp system.
candidates.test_case: Check the Y-system configuration and apply the 60 % / 75 mm check across the interdependent lamps.
candidates.applies_because: Being part of a 'Y' interdependent lamp system is an open option for the lamp.

candidates.text: In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) of each lamp function shall not be intentionally varied while the lamp is switched ON.
candidates.test_case: Monitor intensity, colour and lit surface over time with the function switched ON.
candidates.applies_because: The rear position, stop and reversing lamps are steady-burning lamps.

candidates.text: The photometric characteristics of a lamp function may vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation complies with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
candidates.test_case: Measure intensity in each operating state and check it against the R148 limits for the function.
candidates.applies_because: Variable intensity or reciprocal incorporation (e.g. position/stop sharing LEDs) are open options.

candidates.text: Red light emitted by the rear position lamp, stop lamp and rear retro-reflector shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Observe from the front of the vehicle with the red functions switched ON.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp emits red light at the rear of the vehicle.

candidates.text: There shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of the red lamp functions for an observer moving within Zone 1 (between 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground, bounded laterally by planes at 15° outwards from the vehicle overall width) in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle.
candidates.test_case: Visual check from Zone 1 at 25 m in front of the vehicle, or CAD sight-line analysis per Annex 4.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp contains red rear lamp functions.

candidates.text: In case of doubt, the no-red-light-to-the-front requirement is deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of red light emitted to the front, as verified during lamp type approval, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.
candidates.test_case: Measure the red luminous intensity emitted in forward directions by the lamp and confirm it is ≤ 0.25 cd.
candidates.applies_because: This is the fall-back criterion for the lamp's red functions.

candidates.text: The electrical connections shall be such that the rear position lamps can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously with the front position lamps, end-outline and side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp.
candidates.test_case: Operate the lighting switch and verify that rear position lamps switch together with the other listed lamps.
candidates.applies_because: The lamp includes a rear position lamp function.

candidates.text: The simultaneous switching requirement does not apply while the rear position lamps are switched ON as parking lamps, while daytime running lamps are switched ON, or while the front position lamp function is substituted under paragraph 5.12.1.
